payload.claim: The spec cites `saffron/gates/core/revert.py:261` for the claim that `revert` treats a name collected at head and not at base as a new test. Line 261 is actually `declared = {c.witness for c in acceptance}`; the set arithmetic computing "collected at head and not at base" (`set(after) - set(before)`) sits on line 262, the line immediately below. This is a one-line citation slip in explanatory context prose (the "Out of scope" discussion of #1099), not an instruction the cell acts on and not a line the cell is told to reuse or match verbatim, so it cannot cause a wrong build. It costs nothing to leave for the operator.
